outcome: neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) hospitalization admission
cohort: The study included 60 pregnant women undergoing cesarean myomectomy at Imam Khomeini Hospital in Ahvaz from March 2021 to March 2024.
finding: The study found a considerable incidence of unfavorable maternal and neonatal outcomes following cesarean myomectomy, including blood transfusion (13%), PPH (7%), NICU hospitalization (32%), and growth below the 3rd percentile (12%), with myoma size significantly correlated with blood transfusion rates (P = 0.04).
mod_finding: The study specifically investigated and found a considerable incidence of unfavorable maternal and neonatal outcomes associated with cesarean myomectomy, highlighting risks like blood transfusion, PPH, and neonatal complications related to this mode of birth and surgical procedure.
